title: session-affinity-and-temporal-consistency-playbook-2026
author: Aisha Raman
body:
Overview

This playbook defines session-affinity semantics and temporal consistency guarantees for Redwood's multi-variant, streaming inference layer. It standardizes how inference requests that belong to a logical session (chat or streaming synthesis) are routed, cached, and routed back to compatible runtime shards while balancing latency, throughput, and staleness risk.

Goals
- Provide deterministic developer-facing session guarantees for: prefix caching, KV re-use, and streaming continuity.
- Minimize cross-shard state transfers to preserve p99 latency and reduce token-unit cost.
- Offer operational guidance for rollout, observability, failure modes, and testing.

Scope
- Applies to hosted and dedicated serving modes that support streaming generation and KV caches.
- Excludes long-lived offline batch scoring and non-streaming inference jobs.

Definitions
- Session: logical interaction with an identifier (session_id) representing a conversational context or long-running stream.
- Affinity Key: hash(session_id + user_tenant + model_variant) used for routing.
- Temporal Consistency Window (TCW): configured duration during which cached KV and prefix state must be preferred over cold routing to preserve generation quality.
- Staleness: wall-clock difference between cached KV creation time and the current request; measured in seconds.

Service Level Expectations (SLEs)
- Latency: p99 streaming head latency for sessions assigned to an active affinity shard should be <= 150ms for short responses (<= 64 tokens).
- Affinity hit rate: target >= 92% for active sessions during normal load.
- Max tolerated staleness: default 30 minutes (1800 seconds); configurable by workload.

Affinity Model and Routing Contract
1) Affinity Key construction (must be part of the client request envelope):
   - session_id: UUID (recommended) or provider-assigned string.
   - tenant_id: string.
   - model_variant: e.g., "gptx-8k-quant-v2".
   - affinity_key = sha256("session_id|tenant_id|model_variant").

2) Routing semantics:
   - Strong affinity: within TCW, the control plane will prefer routing to the node that holds a valid KV cache matching affinity_key.
   - Soft affinity: if strong-affinity node is under heavy load or unavailable, fallback routing is allowed to compatible model_variant with a degraded quality flag returned in response metadata.
   - Affinity TTL: default 60 minutes for active sessions; idle eviction after 15 minutes of inactivity unless pinned.

3) Sticky session handoff:
   - When a session is moved (scale, preemption), the runtime will offer a handoff token: {handoff_shard_id, kv_checkpoint_uri, handoff_seq}.
   - New shard may prefetch kv_checkpoint (background) and apply incremental replay up to the handoff_seq before accepting weight-bearing requests.
   - Clients should be able to pass handoff_token in subsequent requests for faster convergence; presence is advisory, not required.

KV Cache Consistency and Invalidation
- Write-through pattern: runtime persists canonical KV snapshots to blob storage (encrypted) after every major interaction or when size thresholds are exceeded.
- Checkpoint cadence: default snapshot every 128 tokens or every 30s, whichever comes first.
- Invalidation triggers:
  - Explicit: client issues session.invalidate(session_id).
  - Time-based: TCW expiry or affinity TTL expiry.
  - Model variant change: unless declared compatible, caches are invalidated across major model architecture changes.

Quality and Degradation Signals
- Responses must include metadata headers in streaming and non-streaming flows:
  - X-Redwood-Affinity: hit|miss|handoff|fallback
  - X-Redwood-Max-Staleness: <seconds>
  - X-Redwood-Variant-Fallback: <variant-id> (if applicable)
- Clients relying on strict context fidelity should treat affinity:miss as a signal to re-send recent tokens as deterministic evidence.

Telemetry and Observability Requirements
- Metrics to emit (names and descriptions):
  - session.affinity.hit_rate: ratio of requests routed to a shard with matching KV available.
  - session.kv.checkpoint_latency_ms: time to persist KV snapshot.
  - session.kv.staleness_seconds: distribution of KV staleness at request handling.
  - session.routing.handoff_count: number of handoffs performed per minute.
  - session.quality.regression_alert: boolean flag emitted by offline eval when post-rollout degradation is detected.
- Traces: include affinity_key, shard_id, kv_checkpoint_uri, and handoff_seq as structured tags.
- Logs: structured events for handshake, prefetch success/failure, eviction, and explicit invalidation by client.

Operational Runbook (Incident flow)
1) Symptom: sudden drop in session.affinity.hit_rate < 70% with correlated p99 latency > 2x baseline.
2) Initial steps:
   a) Check runtime shard health dashboard; identify nodes with elevated cpu/gpu_utilization or oom_kills.
   b) Examine session.routing.handoff_count spikes and recent preemption events.
   c) If handoff backlog exists, trigger emergency prefetch to warm top-10 affected shards.
3) Mitigation options:
   - Short term: lift strict affinity and enable soft-affinity fallback to reduce queueing (config flag: runtime.affinity.soft_fallback=true).
   - Medium term: scale dedicated pools for the affected model_variant and increase checkpointing parallelism.
   - Long term: tune TCW and affinity TTL for workload (examples below).
4) Post-incident: run automated fidelity checks (regression evals against golden prompt set).

Testing and Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests: affinity key generation, handoff token serialization, checkpointing triggers.
- Integration tests: simulate preemption and handoff, assert that end-to-end latency spike < 3x and no more than 5% sessions lose > 5 tokens of context.
- Load tests: maintain affinity hit rate >= 90% at 70% cluster utilization on representative traffic.
- Quality gates: automated evaluation harness must show no >1.5% drop in generation quality (BLEU/ROUGE/BLEU-like or domain-specific metrics) for canary against baseline.

Backward/Forward Compatibility
- Affinity protocol is additive: new headers (X-Redwood-*) are optional and ignored by older clients.
- Any schema bump that changes affinity_key construction must be governed by an ADR and a two-stage rollout with a translation shim for 30 days.

Rollout Plan
1) Phase 0 – Internal lab: unit + integration verification (2 weeks).
2) Phase 1 – Canary (5% traffic) against low-risk tenants; monitor session.affinity.hit_rate, p99 latency, and quality regression alerts for 72 hours.
3) Phase 2 – Gradual ramp to 50% over 5 days with automated abort conditions (quality regression alert OR p99 latency > 2x baseline OR affinity hit rate < 80%).
4) Phase 3 – Global rollout with post-deployment evaluation and documentation update.

Configuration Defaults and Examples
| config_key | default | description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| runtime.affinity.tcw_seconds | 1800 | Temporal consistency window in seconds |
| runtime.affinity.ttl_minutes | 60 | Affinity sticky TTL for active sessions |
| runtime.kv.checkpoint_tokens | 128 | Tokens between write checkpoints |
| runtime.kv.checkpoint_parallelism | 4 | Parallel writers per shard |

Failure Modes and Safeguards
- Preemption storms: implement backpressure on handoff generation and a leaky-bucket limiter for prefetch to blob storage.
- Blob storage throttling: if checkpoint writes fail with 5xx, mark snapshots as transient and increase checkpoint cadence to reduce write size; emit session.kv.checkpoint_error_rate.
- Cross-tenant affinity collision: include tenant_id in affinity_key; collisions must be logged and cause immediate invalidation of the offending session_id.

Ownership and Change Control
- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime (runtime-affinity-steering subteam).
- Change process: any change to affinity_key construction or TCW defaults requires an ADR + interop test matrix and an additional sign-off from Observability and Product.

References and Related Pages
- Runtime cache invalidation and staleness mitigation playbook (see related_pages).
- Adaptive KV coordinator contract.
- Telemetry ingestion and alerting standards.

Appendix: Example Request Envelope
{ "session_id": "0b9f4d3e-8d2a-4b6a-9c3a-2f1d5f6b7c8e", "tenant_id": "acme-corp", "model_variant": "redwood-llm-v1-8k", "affinity_hint": "sha256(...)", "client_metadata": { "region": "us-west-2", "sdk_version": "js-1.4.0" } }

Notes
- This playbook is intentionally pragmatic: it opts for controlled handoffs and advisory tokens rather than synchronous streaming state transfers that would increase tail latency.
- Teams should review these defaults yearly or when traffic patterns change significantly.
